sos_elephant_tag: Elephant near farm / crop damage / danger

sos_assessment_desc: Select quick answers to help authorities prioritize the emergency response:
sos_danger_immediate_sub: People or children are nearby and threatened
sos_animal_present: Animal is currently present on the farm
sos_animal_present_sub: Visible right now in fields or boundary
sos_damage_ongoing_sub: Sugarcane, banana, tomatoes, or drip pipes damaged
sos_safety_elephant: Stay at a safe distance (at least 150m) from elephants. Do not shine flashlights directly into their eyes or make loud sudden noises. Keep farm perimeter lights ON and retreat to a reinforced building.
sos_safety_boar: Do not corner or chase wild boars; females with piglets can charge aggressively. Avoid walking through dense sugarcane or tall crops alone until forest patrol arrives.
sos_safety_leopard: Immediate Threat: Move children and livestock indoors immediately. Lock cattle sheds. Do not crouch or bend down in open fields. Keep lights on and stay inside until forest guards arrive.
sos_safety_bear: Do not run if you spot a sloth bear. Slowly back away without turning your back. Avoid sudden hand movements and make steady, calm human voices so it knows your position and moves away.
sos_safety_snake: Do not attempt to catch or kill the snake. Keep pets and family members away. If someone is bitten, keep the bitten limb immobile below heart level and proceed immediately to the nearest Taluk Hospital for Anti-Snake Venom (ASV).
sos_safety_fire: Move away from the smoke direction. Turn off farm electricity mains and fuel engines. If safe, create a cleared buffer break between dry crops and farm sheds.
sos_safety_default: Stay at a safe distance from the threat. Do not approach or provoke wild animals. Move to a secure location and await guidance from verified government authorities.
